questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Equation of a Trendline
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/1c9f30692222eaaed4cda6b608dcc1ccb01eefd6b5fa7730b5b8bb29c9f528b1.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,2)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,8).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{7-2} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=\frac{6}{5}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{6}{5}x+b \\ 2 & =\frac{6}{5}(2)+b \\ 2 & =\frac{12}{5}+b \\ 10 & =12+5b \\ -2 & =5b \\ b & =-\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x-\frac{2}{5}.
$$

Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(0,9)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,3).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-9}{7-0} \\  & =\frac{-6}{7} \\  & =-\frac{6}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-\frac{6}{7}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(0,9):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{6}{7}x+b \\ 9 & =-\frac{6}{7}(0)+b \\ 9 & =0+b \\ b & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+9.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
y = - x + 1.
